components.note: 广 (shelter) — a building, as in 店, 床, 度: hemp stalks drying in a shed. 麻 also gives sound to 磨 mó, 摩 mó and 魔 mó.

example.hanzi: 我的腿麻了。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de tuǐ má le.
example.english: My leg has gone numb.
example.fact: 麻 covers hemp and also 'numb, tingling', as when a limb falls asleep. It sits inside very common words such as 麻烦 (trouble), 麻将 (mahjong) and 麻辣 (numbing-and-spicy, the Sichuan flavour).

examples.hanzi: 我坐了很久，腿有点发麻。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuò le hěn jiǔ, tuǐ yǒudiǎn fāmá.
examples.english: I have been sitting too long and my foot has gone numb.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的麻婆豆腐很好吃。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de mápó dòufu hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: The mapo tofu at this restaurant is delicious.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — marks money and trade, as in 财, 货, 贵; 赖 is to depend on, or to default on a debt.
剌 (là) hints at the sound: 赖 lài is close, as in 癞 lài and 籁 lài.

example.hanzi: 别赖我，不是我弄坏的。
example.pinyin: Bié lài wǒ, bú shì wǒ nòng huài de.
example.english: Don't blame me, I'm not the one who broke it.
example.fact: 赖 shows up in 赖账 (to refuse to pay a debt), 无赖 (rogue) and 依赖 (to depend on). In speech, 赖 someone means to pin the blame on them unfairly, and 赖在某处 means to hang around and refuse to leave.

examples.hanzi: 他欠了钱，还想赖账。
examples.pinyin: Tā qiàn le qián, hái xiǎng làizhàng.
examples.english: He owes money and still wants to deny the debt.

examples.hanzi: 小狗总是赖在我身边不走。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu zǒngshì lài zài wǒ shēnbiān bù zǒu.
examples.english: The puppy always clings to my side and will not leave.

components.note: 目 (eye) — marks seeing and watching, as in 看, 眼, 睡; 督 is to oversee, to watch over.
叔 (shū) is a loose hint for dū.

example.hanzi: 老师督促我们每天复习。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī dūcù wǒmen měitiān fùxí.
example.english: The teacher urges us to review every day.
example.fact: 督 is a bound form found in 督促 (to urge), 监督 (to supervise) and 总督 (governor-general). It also appears in 基督, the Chinese rendering of 'Christ', so 基督教 means Christianity.

examples.hanzi: 经理每天都要监督工作进度。
examples.pinyin: Jīnglǐ měitiān dōu yào jiāndū gōngzuò jìndù.
examples.english: The manager has to monitor the work progress every day.

examples.hanzi: 妈妈总是督促我多读书。
examples.pinyin: Māma zǒngshì dūcù wǒ duō dúshū.
examples.english: Mom is always urging me to read more.

components.note: 女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐.
昏 (hūn, dusk) gives the exact sound; weddings were traditionally held at dusk, so the sound clue is also a meaning clue.
纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — fine threads and cloth; also in 红 red, 级 level.
少 (shǎo) is a loose clue; it also sounds out 沙 shā (sand) and 砂 shā.

example.hanzi: 新娘穿着白色的婚纱。
example.pinyin: Xīnniáng chuānzhuó báisè de hūnshā.
example.english: The bride wore a white wedding dress.
example.fact: White wedding dresses became fashionable largely after Queen Victoria wore one, rather than the traditional royal silver, at her 1840 wedding to Prince Albert. Before that, brides of most backgrounds commonly wore whatever good dress they owned, in any color, so it could be reused afterward.

examples.hanzi: 她的婚纱是妈妈亲手做的。
examples.pinyin: Tā de hūnshā shì māma qīnshǒu zuò de.
examples.english: Her wedding dress was made by her mother herself.

examples.hanzi: 新娘正在试穿婚纱。
examples.pinyin: Xīnniáng zhèngzài shìchuān hūnshā.
examples.english: The bride is trying on her wedding dress.

components.note: 土 (earth) — 土 is earth and ground, as in 地, 城, 块; 坦 is level ground, then open and frank.
旦 (dàn) — near sound — 坦 is tǎn; 旦 also sounds out 但 dàn and 担 dān.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.

example.hanzi: 一辆坦克缓缓驶过。
example.pinyin: Yī liàng tǎnkè huǎnhuǎn shǐguò.
example.english: A tank slowly drove past.
example.fact: The first tanks saw combat at the Battle of the Somme in September 1916, and were code-named 'tanks' during development and shipping so that factory workers and spies would mistake the crates for water-storage containers headed to Russia. The disguise name stuck even after the vehicles' true purpose became obvious on the battlefield.

examples.hanzi: 博物馆里展出了一辆旧坦克。
examples.pinyin: Bówùguǎn lǐ zhǎnchūle yí liàng jiù tǎnkè.
examples.english: An old tank is on display in the museum.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们很喜欢玩具坦克。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen hěn xǐhuan wánjù tǎnkè.
examples.english: Children love toy tanks.

components.note: 風 (traditional wind) — 风 is the simplified form of 風, which had 凡 (fán) as a loose sound hint around 虫; the simplified shape is just a reduced form.
走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 起, 越, 赶: going toward something that attracts you.
取 (qǔ) is a close sound clue for qù; 取 also in 娶 qǔ and 聚 jù.

example.hanzi: 他说话很风趣，大家都喜欢和他聊天。
example.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà hěn fēngqù, dàjiā dōu xǐhuan hé tā liáotiān.
example.english: He is witty when he speaks, and everyone likes chatting with him.
example.fact: Mark Twain's sharp, understated wit made him one of the most quoted writers in the English language, with lines still repeated more than a century after his death in 1910. He reportedly kept a running scrapbook of clippings and notes just to track his own jokes and observations for reuse.

examples.hanzi: 他讲话风趣,总能把大家逗笑。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiǎnghuà fēngqù, zǒng néng bǎ dàjiā dòuxiào.
examples.english: He's witty and always makes everyone laugh.

examples.hanzi: 这位老师的课风趣幽默,学生们都爱听。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi lǎoshī de kè fēngqù yōumò, xuéshengmen dōu ài tīng.
examples.english: This teacher's classes are funny, and students love them.

components.note: 首 (head, first) — a picture of a head with hair on top, which became the word for first and chief: 首先, 元首, also a measure for songs.
目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.

example.hanzi: 英国首相住在唐宁街十号。
example.pinyin: Yīngguó shǒuxiàng zhù zài Tángníng Jiē shí hào.
example.english: The British Prime Minister lives at 10 Downing Street.
example.fact: Winston Churchill is the only British Prime Minister to have won a Nobel Prize in Literature rather than Peace, awarded in 1953 largely for his historical writing and wartime speeches. He had been nominated for the Peace Prize multiple times over the years but never won it.

examples.hanzi: 首相今天在电视上发表了讲话。
examples.pinyin: Shǒuxiàng jīntiān zài diànshì shàng fābiǎole jiǎnghuà.
examples.english: The prime minister gave a speech on TV today.

examples.hanzi: 日本首相明天将访问中国。
examples.pinyin: Rìběn shǒuxiàng míngtiān jiāng fǎngwèn Zhōngguó.
examples.english: The Japanese prime minister will visit China tomorrow.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech: 说, 话, 请; 诞 first meant big talk, then birth and birthday.
延 (yán) is only a loose sound hint for dàn.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.hanzi: 这个理论诞生于二十世纪初。
example.pinyin: Zhège lǐlùn dànshēng yú èrshí shìjì chū.
example.english: This theory was born in the early 20th century.
example.fact: The World Wide Web was born between 1989 and 1991, when physicist Tim Berners-Lee, working at CERN, wrote the first web browser, the first web server, and the first webpage to help researchers share documents. Fewer than a dozen websites existed by the end of 1992; today there are well over a billion.

examples.hanzi: 我们家今天诞生了一个小宝宝。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā jīntiān dànshēngle yí gè xiǎo bǎobao.
examples.english: A little baby was born in our family today.

examples.hanzi: 这个品牌诞生在一个小车库里。
examples.pinyin: Zhège pǐnpái dànshēng zài yí gè xiǎo chēkù lǐ.
examples.english: This brand was born in a small garage.

components.note: 孚 (a hand over a child) — the usual reading is a mother nursing her child, hence breast and milk.

example.hanzi: 婴儿最好喝母乳。
example.pinyin: Yīng'ér zuì hǎo hē mǔrǔ.
example.english: Babies are best fed breast milk.
example.fact: 乳 is the formal word for milk: 乳制品 (dairy products), 乳酸 (lactic acid), 乳房 (breast). In daily speech people say 牛奶 for a glass of cow's milk, reserving 乳 for written, technical or medical contexts.

examples.hanzi: 医生建议孩子多吃乳制品。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng jiànyì háizi duō chī rǔzhìpǐn.
examples.english: The doctor suggests that kids eat more dairy products.

examples.hanzi: 早上我喜欢喝一杯牛乳。
examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang wǒ xǐhuan hē yì bēi niúrǔ.
examples.english: I like having a glass of milk in the morning.

components.note: 歹 (bad bone) — death and decay, as in 残 remnant, 烈 fierce, 殊 special.
匕 (person) — a person beside bones: death.
礻 (altar, spirit — form of 示) — gods, rites and blessings: 礼 ritual, 福 fortune, 祝 wish; here 神 god or spirit.
申 (shēn) gives the sound (shén, tone differs); also in 伸 shēn stretch and 绅 shēn.

example.hanzi: 传说中死神会带走逝者的灵魂。
example.pinyin: Chuánshuō zhōng sǐshén huì dàizǒu shìzhě de línghún.
example.english: Legend says death takes away the souls of the deceased.
example.fact: The hooded, scythe-carrying 'Grim Reaper' image took shape in European art during and after the Black Death of 1347-1351, a plague that killed an estimated 25 to 50 million people, roughly a third of Europe's population. Constant, visible mortality on that scale pushed death itself into becoming a recurring, personified figure in paintings and woodcuts of the era.

examples.hanzi: 故事里的死神穿着一件黑色的长袍。
examples.pinyin: Gùshi lǐ de sǐshén chuānzhe yí jiàn hēisè de chángpáo.
examples.english: The Grim Reaper in the story wears a long black robe.

examples.hanzi: 他躲过了死神,从病中恢复了过来。
examples.pinyin: Tā duǒguòle sǐshén, cóng bìng zhōng huīfùle guòlái.
examples.english: He escaped death and recovered from his illness.

components.note: 今 (jīn) — the top part hints the sound — 金 is jīn, like 今; 金 means gold and metal.
金 (metal) — as a radical it shrinks to 钅 in simplified characters — 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 银 silver.
⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.

example.hanzi: 夕阳把天空染成了金色。
example.pinyin: Xīyáng bǎ tiānkōng rǎnchéng le jīnsè.
example.english: The setting sun dyed the sky golden.
example.fact: Gold is so chemically unreactive that it almost never corrodes or tarnishes, which is why an estimated 244,000 tonnes of gold ever mined throughout human history — nearly all of it — still exists today in some form, from jewelry to coins to circuit boards. Melted down, all of it would fit into a cube roughly 22 meters on each side.

examples.hanzi: 她的头发是金色的,像阳光一样。
examples.pinyin: Tā de tóufa shì jīnsè de, xiàng yángguāng yíyàng.
examples.english: Her hair is golden, like sunshine.

examples.hanzi: 秋天,田里一片金色。
examples.pinyin: Qiūtiān, tián lǐ yí piàn jīnsè.
examples.english: In autumn, the fields are a sea of gold.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 适 is to go to what suits you. 舌 is a simplification stand-in, not a real clue.
當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).

example.hanzi: 请选择适当的时间开会。
example.pinyin: Qǐng xuǎnzé shìdàng de shíjiān kāihuì.
example.english: Please choose an appropriate time for the meeting.
example.fact: Astronomers use the term 'Goldilocks zone' for the orbital region around a star where temperatures are just right for liquid water to exist on a planet's surface — not too hot, not too cold. The term borrows from the children's story and has become standard shorthand in the search for potentially habitable exoplanets.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服的大小很适当,不会太紧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu de dàxiǎo hěn shìdàng, bú huì tài jǐn.
examples.english: The size of this garment is just right and not too tight.

examples.hanzi: 运动要适当,不能一下子太累。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòng yào shìdàng, bù néng yíxiàzi tài lèi.
examples.english: Exercise in moderation; don't overdo it all at once.

components.note: 心 (heart) — loyalty is of the heart, as in 想 think, 爱 love, 思; 心 sits at the bottom.
中 (zhōng) gives the sound exactly: 忠 zhōng, also in 钟 zhōng.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室: a house stocked with goods, so solid and real.

example.hanzi: 狗是人类忠实的朋友。
example.pinyin: Gǒu shì rénlèi zhōngshí de péngyǒu.
example.english: Dogs are humans' faithful friends.
example.fact: In 1920s Tokyo, an Akita dog named Hachikō continued walking to Shibuya Station every day for nearly ten years after his owner died suddenly at work, waiting for a return that never came. A bronze statue of Hachikō still stands outside the station today, and the story remains one of Japan's best-known examples of animal loyalty.

examples.hanzi: 她是一个忠实的读者,每期杂志都买。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè zhōngshí de dúzhě, měi qī zázhì dōu mǎi.
examples.english: She's a loyal reader who buys every issue of the magazine.

examples.hanzi: 这部电影忠实地还原了原著的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng zhōngshí de huányuánle yuánzhù de gùshi.
examples.english: This film faithfully recreates the story of the original book.

meanings: to enjoy (i.e. have the use or benefit of)

components.note: 享 (enjoy) — a picture of an ancestral hall where offerings were shared, hence to enjoy; it also appears in 亨 hēng and 郭 guō.
用 (use) — early picture is debated: a pail, a fenced enclosure or a hung bell. Memory aid: a door-frame 冂 with a cross-bar — a tool 'put to use' (使用, 不用).

example.hanzi: 我们在花园里享用晚餐。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài huāyuán lǐ xiǎngyòng wǎncān.
example.english: We enjoyed dinner in the garden.
example.fact: The formal 'service à la russe' dining style, which serves courses to guests one at a time in sequence rather than piling every dish onto the table at once, spread through European aristocratic banquets in the 19th century. That sequential format is the direct ancestor of the multi-course restaurant meal most diners enjoy today.

examples.hanzi: 请大家慢慢享用,不够再添。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng dàjiā mànmàn xiǎngyòng, bú gòu zài tiān.
examples.english: Please enjoy it slowly, and we'll add more if it's not enough.

examples.hanzi: 游客可以免费享用酒店的早餐。
examples.pinyin: Yóukè kěyǐ miǎnfèi xiǎngyòng jiǔdiàn de zǎocān.
examples.english: Guests can enjoy the hotel's breakfast for free.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — marks speech, sounds and eating, as in 叫 call, 吃 eat, 唱 sing; 呗 is a sentence-final particle.
贝 (bèi) — close sound: 呗 bei. 贝 also sounds out 狈 bèi.

example.hanzi: 不会就学呗。
example.pinyin: Bù huì jiù xué bei.
example.english: If you can't do it, just learn it, then.
example.fact: Sentence-final 呗 (bei) conveys that something is obvious or no big deal, often with a hint of 'so what?'. It is chatty and a bit casual, unlike 吧, which softens a suggestion. The original reading bài is the 'chant' in 梵呗, Buddhist chanting.

examples.hanzi: 想去就去呗，别犹豫了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎng qù jiù qù bei, bié yóuyù le.
examples.english: If you want to go, just go. Don't hesitate.

examples.hanzi: 喜欢就买呗，价格不贵。
examples.pinyin: Xǐhuan jiù mǎi bei, jiàgé bú guì.
examples.english: If you like it, just buy it. It is not expensive.

components.note: 疒 (illness) — marks sickness, as in 病 ill, 疼 pain, 痛 ache; 痒 is itching.
羊 (yáng) — close sound: 痒 yǎng. 羊 also sounds out 洋 yáng and 样 yàng.

example.hanzi: 我的背很痒。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de bèi hěn yǎng.
example.english: My back is very itchy.
example.fact: 痒 combines with other words: 发痒 (to itch), 挠痒 (to scratch an itch), and 怕痒 (to be ticklish). 手痒 literally 'hands itch' means you are itching to try or join in, such as playing a game.

examples.hanzi: 蚊子咬了我，我的腿很痒。
examples.pinyin: Wénzi yǎo le wǒ, wǒ de tuǐ hěn yǎng.
examples.english: A mosquito bit me and my leg is very itchy.

examples.hanzi: 别挠我，我怕痒痒！
examples.pinyin: Bié náo wǒ, wǒ pà yǎngyang!
examples.english: Don't tickle me. I am ticklish!

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding on.
寺 (sì) is a loose sound clue for chí; 寺 also in 诗 shī, 待 dài, 特 tè and 等 děng.

example.hanzi: 请持票入场。
example.pinyin: Qǐng chí piào rù chǎng.
example.english: Please enter with your ticket in hand.
example.fact: 持 rarely stands alone in conversation, but it is the core of many everyday words: 支持 (support), 坚持 (persist), 保持 (keep, maintain) and 持续 (continue). On signs, 持 + object means 'holding/with', as in 持证 (holding a pass).

examples.hanzi: 他一只手持着雨伞，一只手拿着包。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì zhī shǒu chí zhe yǔsǎn, yì zhī shǒu ná zhe bāo.
examples.english: He holds an umbrella in one hand and carries a bag in the other.

examples.hanzi: 谢谢你一直支持我。
examples.pinyin: Xièxie nǐ yìzhí zhīchí wǒ.
examples.english: Thank you for always supporting me.

components.note: 彳 (step) — the left part and radical, as in 往 and 行. It suggests going step by step; in 微 'tiny', as in 微笑 smile. Rest of the shape is unclear.
攵 (tap) — the bottom-right part, as in 收. Memory aid: tapping very lightly with tiny steps, so everything is 'slight'.

example.hanzi: 她微笑着点了点头。
example.pinyin: Tā wēixiào zhe diǎn le diǎn tóu.
example.english: She nodded with a slight smile.
example.fact: 微 means tiny or slight and works as a prefix: 微笑 (smile), 微波炉 (microwave oven), 微信 (WeChat, literally 'micro-message') and 微博 (microblog). 微 is also the 'micro-' of 微米 (micrometre).

examples.hanzi: 她微微一笑，没有说话。
examples.pinyin: Tā wēiwēi yí xiào, méiyǒu shuōhuà.
examples.english: She smiled slightly and said nothing.

examples.hanzi: 我给朋友发了一条微信。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi péngyou fā le yì tiáo wēixìn.
examples.english: I sent my friend a WeChat message.

components.note: 氵 (water, 三点水) — marks water and liquids, as in 海 sea, 河 river, 汤 soup; 浓 is thick, strong or dense, as in 浓茶.
农 (nóng) — same sound: 浓 nóng. 农 also sounds out 脓 nóng.

example.hanzi: 这杯咖啡太浓了。
example.pinyin: Zhè bēi kāfēi tài nóng le.
example.english: This coffee is too strong.
example.fact: 浓 describes liquids, smells, colours and even feelings: 浓茶 (strong tea), 浓烟 (thick smoke), 浓厚 (strong, as in interest) and 浓情蜜意 (deep affection). Its opposite is 淡 (weak, light).

examples.hanzi: 这杯茶泡得太浓了，我不习惯。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi chá pào de tài nóng le, wǒ bù xíguàn.
examples.english: This tea is brewed too strong.

examples.hanzi: 院子里有浓浓的花香。
examples.pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ yǒu nóngnóng de huāxiāng.
examples.english: The yard is filled with a rich floral scent.

meanings: to indicate clearly and with certainty

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 指 is the finger or to point.
旨 (zhǐ) sounds exactly like 指; also in 脂 zhī.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 老师指定他为班长。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zhǐdìng tā wéi bānzhǎng.
example.english: The teacher appointed him class monitor.
example.fact: In the Roman Republic, a dictator was a legally appointed office, not an illegitimate seizure of power — the Senate could designate one person with sweeping emergency authority, but strictly for a fixed term of six months. That built-in expiration was meant to prevent exactly the kind of permanent one-man rule the word later came to mean.

examples.hanzi: 请在指定的地点交作业。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhǐdìng de dìdiǎn jiāo zuòyè.
examples.english: Please hand in your homework at the designated place.

examples.hanzi: 比赛的规则由老师指定。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài de guīzé yóu lǎoshī zhǐdìng.
examples.english: The rules of the contest are set by the teacher.

components.note: 著 (zhù / zhe) — older form of 着: 艹 plant + 者 (zhě) as sound. 着 is a variant with 羊 over 目; neither part gives the 'in progress' sense.
目 (eye) — the bottom. The eye family: 看, 眼, 睛, 睡. In 着 it is only part of a variant shape. Memory aid: 睡着 — eyes 目 shut, asleep.
阝 (mound, 左耳旁 on the left) — land and hills, as in 院, 阳, 队. The right part is a simplification with no sound clue.

example.hanzi: 那架飞机安全着陆了。
example.pinyin: Nà jià fēijī ānquán zhuólù le.
example.english: That airplane landed safely.
example.fact: The Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 lasted just 12 seconds and covered 120 feet, shorter than the wingspan of a modern Boeing 747. Sixty-six years later, the Apollo 11 lunar module Eagle landed on the Moon's Sea of Tranquility using less onboard computing power than a modern pocket calculator.

examples.hanzi: 飞机在大雾中着陆,乘客们都很紧张。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī zài dàwù zhōng zhuólù, chéngkèmen dōu hěn jǐnzhāng.
examples.english: The plane landed in thick fog, and the passengers were all nervous.

examples.hanzi: 飞机着陆的时候,有一点颠簸。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī zhuólù de shíhou, yǒu yìdiǎn diānbǒ.
examples.english: There was a bit of turbulence when the plane landed.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo, as in 笔, 等, 算: a hollow pipe.
官 (guān) is a close sound clue for guǎn; 官 also in 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 网站管理员每天检查系统日志。
example.pinyin: Wǎngzhàn guǎnlǐyuán měitiān jiǎnchá xìtǒng rìzhì.
example.english: The website administrator checks the system logs every day.
example.fact: Grace Hopper, one of the first computer programmers, popularized the term 'bug' after a moth was found jammed in a relay of the Harvard Mark II computer in 1947, an incident her team literally taped into the logbook. The term stuck and is now standard across the entire software industry.

examples.hanzi: 小区的管理员每天都会巡逻。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoqū de guǎnlǐyuán měitiān dōu huì xúnluó.
examples.english: The neighborhood's superintendent patrols every day.

examples.hanzi: 我忘记密码了,得找管理员重设。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wàngjì mìmǎ le, děi zhǎo guǎnlǐyuán chóngshè.
examples.english: I forgot my password, so I have to ask the administrator to reset it.

components.note: 人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do. 便 is a person adjusting things 更 to make them convenient (traditional explanation).

example.hanzi: 他提前出发,以便赶上火车。
example.pinyin: Tā tíqián chūfā, yǐbiàn gǎnshàng huǒchē.
example.english: He left early so that he could catch the train.
example.fact: The Shinkansen bullet train, launched in Japan in 1964 ahead of the Tokyo Olympics, has carried over 10 billion passengers. In its entire operating history it has never had a passenger fatality caused by a derailment or collision.

examples.hanzi: 请留下你的电话,以便我们联系你。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng liúxià nǐ de diànhuà, yǐbiàn wǒmen liánxì nǐ.
examples.english: Please leave your phone number so we can contact you.

examples.hanzi: 我把书放在桌上,以便明天早上带走。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ shū fàng zài zhuō shàng, yǐbiàn míngtiān zǎoshang dàizǒu.
examples.english: I put the book on the table so I can take it tomorrow morning.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
土 (earth) — 土 is earth, as in 地, 城; a mold was made of clay, so 型 is a model or type.
刑 (xíng) — same sound — 型 is xíng, like 刑.

example.hanzi: 这家工厂生产小型发电机。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng shēngchǎn xiǎoxíng fādiànjī.
example.english: This factory produces small-scale generators.
example.fact: The first practical electric generator, built by Michael Faraday in 1831, was small enough to hold in two hands. It demonstrated the principle of electromagnetic induction that today powers turbines generating gigawatts of electricity worldwide.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个小型的家庭餐馆。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè xiǎoxíng de jiātíng cānguǎn.
examples.english: This is a small family restaurant.

examples.hanzi: 他开着一辆小型卡车送货。
examples.pinyin: Tā kāizhe yí liàng xiǎoxíng kǎchē sòng huò.
examples.english: He drives a small truck to deliver goods.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — ⺮ is bamboo, as in 笔, 筷, 箱; tallies were bamboo slips split in two to match, so 符 is to match.
付 (fù) — near sound — 符 is fú; 付 also sounds out 附 fù and 府 fǔ.
口 (mouth) — speaking, shouting: 叫, 吗, 喊; 号 is to call out, then a call-sign or number.
丂 (kǎo) is only a loose clue; it also appears in 考 kǎo and 巧 qiǎo.

example.hanzi: 数学公式里有很多特殊符号。
example.pinyin: Shùxué gōngshì lǐ yǒu hěnduō tèshū fúhào.
example.english: There are many special symbols in mathematical formulas.
example.fact: The equals sign (=) was invented in 1557 by the Welsh mathematician Robert Recorde. He chose two parallel lines because, in his words, no two things could be more equal.

examples.hanzi: 地图上的这个符号表示公园。
examples.pinyin: Dìtú shàng de zhège fúhào biǎoshì gōngyuán.
examples.english: This symbol on the map stands for a park.

examples.hanzi: 鸽子是和平的符号。
examples.pinyin: Gēzi shì hépíng de fúhào.
examples.english: The dove is a symbol of peace.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — to throw down by hand; also in 打 hit, 扔 throw.
率 (shuài) gives the same syllable with a different tone.
足 (foot, ⻊) — foot actions, as in 跑 run, 跳 jump.
交 (jiāo) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 胶 jiāo and 郊 jiāo.

example.hanzi: 那两个男孩在草地上摔跤。
example.pinyin: Nà liǎng gè nánhái zài cǎodì shàng shuāijiāo.
example.english: Those two boys were wrestling on the grass.
example.fact: Wrestling is depicted in cave paintings over 15,000 years old in Lascaux, France, making it one of the oldest recorded sports in human history. It was also among the original events of the ancient Olympic Games in 708 BC.

examples.hanzi: 小时候我常和哥哥摔跤玩。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎoshíhou wǒ cháng hé gēge shuāijiāo wán.
examples.english: When we were little, my brother and I often wrestled for fun.

examples.hanzi: 下雨天路很滑,他不小心摔跤了。
examples.pinyin: Xiàyǔ tiān lù hěn huá, tā bù xiǎoxīn shuāijiāo le.
examples.english: The road was slippery in the rain and he fell by accident.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 心 marks emotions and thought, as in 想, 思, 急; 怒 is rage.
奴 (nú) — same sound, different tone — 怒 is nù; 奴 also sounds out 努 nǔ.

example.hanzi: 他怒气冲冲地走了。
example.pinyin: Tā nùqì chōngchōng de zǒu le.
example.english: He left in a towering rage.
example.fact: 怒 is stronger and more literary than 生气: 发怒 (fly into a rage), 愤怒 (indignant), 怒火 (flames of anger). It also describes flowers in 怒放, 'blooming with abandon'.

examples.hanzi: 看到孩子撒谎，他非常愤怒。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào háizi sāhuǎng, tā fēicháng fènnù.
examples.english: Seeing the child lie, he was very angry.

examples.hanzi: 你别发怒，我们慢慢谈。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bié fānù, wǒmen mànmàn tán.
examples.english: Don't lose your temper. Let's talk calmly.

components.note: 工 (tool, work) — originally a carpenter's square held in a hand — the same word as 矩; 巨 also sounds out 距 jù and 拒 jù.

example.hanzi: 这是一个巨大的惊喜。
example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè jùdà de jīngxǐ.
example.english: This is a huge surprise.
example.fact: 巨 mostly appears in compounds: 巨大 (enormous), 巨人 (giant), 巨星 (superstar) and 巨额 (a huge sum). Young people also use it as a casual intensifier, as in 巨好吃 'insanely tasty'.

examples.hanzi: 这棵树的树干特别巨大。
examples.pinyin: Zhè kē shù de shùgàn tèbié jùdà.
examples.english: The trunk of this tree is extremely huge.

examples.hanzi: 他为这个项目花了巨款。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèi zhège xiàngmù huā le jùkuǎn.
examples.english: He spent a huge sum on this project.

components.note: 方 (square, direction) — in 旗 it marks flags and banners, as in 旅 travel, 族 clan; 旗 is a flag.
其 (qí) — same sound: 旗 qí. 其 also sounds out 期 qī and 棋 qí.

example.hanzi: 那面旗是红色的。
example.pinyin: Nà miàn qí shì hóngsè de.
example.english: That flag is red.
example.fact: The measure word for flags is 面 (miàn): 一面旗. 旗 also appears in 旗袍 (qipao), literally 'banner robe', named after the Manchu 'banner' (旗) people who wore the original form.

examples.hanzi: 广场上挂着很多彩旗。
examples.pinyin: Guǎngchǎng shàng guà zhe hěn duō cǎiqí.
examples.english: Many colorful flags hang in the square.

examples.hanzi: 升旗仪式在早上八点开始。
examples.pinyin: Shēngqí yíshì zài zǎoshang bā diǎn kāishǐ.
examples.english: The flag-raising ceremony begins at eight in the morning.

components.note: 金 (metal) — ancient mirrors were bronze, hence 鉴 is a mirror and to examine; as 钅 in 钱 money, 铁 iron.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 安 safe, 客 guest; settling down under a roof.
正 (zhèng, upright; the lower part is written 疋) is a loose sound clue for dìng; also in 证 zhèng and 政 zhèng.

example.hanzi: 专家对这件古董进行了鉴定。
example.pinyin: Zhuānjiā duì zhè jiàn gǔdǒng jìnxíngle jiàndìng.
example.english: The expert appraised this antique.
example.fact: In 1961, art experts using X-ray and pigment analysis proved that a supposed Vermeer painting, 'Christ and the Adulteress,' was actually a 20th-century forgery. It had been painted by Han van Meegeren, who sold it to Nazi official Hermann Göring during World War II.

examples.hanzi: 这幅画需要专家来鉴定真假。
examples.pinyin: Zhè fú huà xūyào zhuānjiā lái jiàndìng zhēnjiǎ.
examples.english: This painting needs an expert to authenticate whether it's real.

examples.hanzi: 医生对他的伤情做了鉴定。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng duì tā de shāngqíng zuòle jiàndìng.
examples.english: The doctor assessed his injury.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 他, 做, 作; 仿 is to imitate someone.
方 (fāng) hints at the sound: 仿 fǎng is close, as in 访 fǎng and 纺 fǎng.
亻 (person) — Buddha is a person; the same part marks people, as in 仙 immortal, 你 you.
弗 (fú) gives the sound as in 仿佛 fǎng fú; it also sounds out 费 fèi and 拂 fú.

example.hanzi: 她仿佛听到了远处的雷声。
example.pinyin: Tā fǎngfú tīngdàole yuǎnchù de léishēng.
example.english: She seemed to hear thunder in the distance.
example.fact: Thunder is the sound of air rapidly expanding after being heated by a lightning bolt to temperatures hotter than the surface of the sun, around 30,000 Kelvin. Because light travels far faster than sound, counting the seconds between a flash and its thunder reveals roughly how many miles away the strike occurred.

examples.hanzi: 他仿佛变了一个人,说话都不一样了。
examples.pinyin: Tā fǎngfú biànle yí gè rén, shuōhuà dōu bù yíyàng le.
examples.english: He seems like a different person; even the way he talks has changed.

examples.hanzi: 走进老房子,我仿佛回到了童年。
examples.pinyin: Zǒujìn lǎo fángzi, wǒ fǎngfú huídàole tóngnián.
examples.english: Walking into the old house, it felt as if I'd returned to childhood.

components.note: 氵 (water) — liquids and flowing; 没 first meant sink or submerge (淹没), which led to "gone" and then "not have".
殳 (shū) is only a loose sound hint for 没 (méi/mò); it also sits in 设 shè and 投 tóu.
攵 (tap, strike) — hand with stick, as in 教, 改, 放: to gather by force or hand.
丩 (jiū) is only a loose sound clue for shōu.

example.hanzi: 海关没收了他携带的违禁品。
example.pinyin: Hǎiguān mòshōule tā xiédài de wéijìnpǐn.
example.english: Customs confiscated the contraband he was carrying.
example.fact: In 2019, Chinese customs officials confiscated more than 700 kilograms of elephant ivory hidden inside shipping containers labeled as timber. It was part of a global enforcement effort against wildlife trafficking that intensified after China's domestic ivory trade ban took effect in 2018.

examples.hanzi: 老师没收了学生上课玩的手机。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī mòshōule xuésheng shàngkè wán de shǒujī.
examples.english: The teacher confiscated the phone the student was playing with in class.

examples.hanzi: 警察没收了他的非法所得。
examples.pinyin: Jǐngchá mòshōule tā de fēifǎ suǒdé.
examples.english: The police seized his illegal gains.

components.note: 必 (bì) is a sound clue for 秘 mì, 密 mì and 蜜 mì: the same series, with only the initial changing.
雨 (rain) — weather, as in 雪 snow, 雷 thunder, 零 zero. Oldest form: a person waiting out rain; waiting turned into "need".
而 (ér) is only a loose sound hint here; 需 also sounds out 须 xū.

example.hanzi: 水是人类生存必需的资源。
example.pinyin: Shuǐ shì rénlèi shēngcún bìxū de zīyuán.
example.english: Water is a resource essential to human survival.
example.fact: A human body is roughly 60% water by weight, and a person can typically survive only about three days without any water intake, compared to several weeks without food. Water is required for nearly every cellular process, including regulating body temperature.

examples.hanzi: 旅行时,护照是必需的证件。
examples.pinyin: Lǚxíng shí, hùzhào shì bìxū de zhèngjiàn.
examples.english: When traveling, a passport is a necessary document.

examples.hanzi: 学好一门语言必需多练习。
examples.pinyin: Xuéhǎo yì mén yǔyán bìxū duō liànxí.
examples.english: To learn a language well, you must practice more.

components.note: 门 (gate) — looking things over at the gate; also in 问 ask, 间 between.
兑 (duì) is a loose clue; 悦 yuè shares it and sounds exactly like 阅.
讠 (speech, from 言) — marks talk and language, as in 说, 语, 话; 读 is to read aloud.
卖 (mài) is only a loose hint for dú; it stands in for an older 賣, as in 牍 dú and 犊 dú.

example.hanzi: 每天阅读半小时对孩子很有好处。
example.pinyin: Měitiān yuèdú bàn xiǎoshí duì háizi hěn yǒu hǎochù.
example.english: Reading for half an hour every day is very good for children.
example.fact: The oldest known library, established by the Assyrian king Ashurbanipal around 630 BC in Nineveh, held over 30,000 clay cuneiform tablets. It has helped modern scholars reconstruct much of ancient Mesopotamian literature and science.

examples.hanzi: 我每天晚上睡前阅读三十分钟。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān wǎnshang shuìqián yuèdú sānshí fēnzhōng.
examples.english: I read for thirty minutes every night before bed.

examples.hanzi: 这篇文章的阅读量已经超过一万了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè piān wénzhāng de yuèdú liàng yǐjīng chāoguò yíwàn le.
examples.english: This article has already been read over ten thousand times.

components.note: 艹 (plants) — marks grasses and flowers, as in 草, 茶, 菜; 花 is a flower.
化 (huà) hints at the sound: 花 huā is close, and 化 also gives 华 huá and 货 huò.
艹 (plants) — marks grasses and flowers, as in 草, 茶, 菜; 花 is a flower.
化 (huà) hints at the sound: 花 huā is close, and 化 also gives 华 huá and 货 huò.

example.hanzi: 他穿着一件花花绿绿的衬衫去参加派对。
example.pinyin: Tā chuānzhuó yī jiàn huāhuā-lǜlǜ de chènshān qù cānjiā pàiduì.
example.english: He wore a flashy, multicolored shirt to the party.
example.fact: Some of the most vividly patterned animals in nature, such as the mandarin fish and the peacock, use bright, multicolored displays for camouflage disruption or mate attraction rather than pure decoration. Biologists call this phenomenon disruptive coloration.

examples.hanzi: 花园里开满了花花绿绿的花。
examples.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ kāimǎnle huāhuā-lǜlǜ de huā.
examples.english: The garden is full of colorful flowers.

examples.hanzi: 小孩穿着花花的裙子,在院子里跳舞。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái chuānzhe huāhuā de qúnzi, zài yuànzi lǐ tiàowǔ.
examples.english: The little girl in a colorful dress is dancing in the yard.

components.note: 亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: a person hurt. The traditional 傷 took its sound from 昜 yáng (also in 汤 and 场).
亡 (die, lose) — dictionary: a man in a coffin; early forms may be a person hiding or fleeing. Treat as a memory aid. It also gives sound clues in 忙 máng, 盲 máng.
亠 (lid) — the top. Memory aid: a lid closed over a person — gone, dead, as in 死亡.

example.hanzi: 这次地震造成了严重的人员伤亡。
example.pinyin: Zhè cì dìzhèn zàochéngle yánzhòng de rényuán shāngwáng.
example.english: This earthquake caused serious casualties.
example.fact: The 1960 Valdivia earthquake in Chile remains the most powerful earthquake ever recorded, measuring 9.5 on the moment magnitude scale. It was strong enough to shift the Earth's axis slightly and even triggered volcanic eruptions weeks later.

examples.hanzi: 这场车祸没有造成人员伤亡。
examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng chēhuò méiyǒu zàochéng rényuán shāngwáng.
examples.english: This car accident caused no casualties.

examples.hanzi: 战争让两边都有很大的伤亡。
examples.pinyin: Zhànzhēng ràng liǎngbiān dōu yǒu hěn dà de shāngwáng.
examples.english: The war caused heavy casualties on both sides.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: guarding with the hands.
户 (hù, door) gives the exact sound; 户 means door or household.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球 ball, 玩 play, 现 appear: 理 first meant polishing jade along its grain, then reason.
里 (lǐ) gives the exact sound; also in 鲤 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 护士每天都要护理病人。
example.pinyin: Hùshi měitiān dōu yào hùlǐ bìngrén.
example.english: Nurses have to care for patients every day.
example.fact: Florence Nightingale, regarded as the founder of modern nursing, dramatically reduced death rates among wounded soldiers during the Crimean War in the 1850s simply by improving hygiene and sanitation in field hospitals. She documented this work using pioneering statistical charts.

examples.hanzi: 她在医院里护理了爷爷半个月。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yīyuàn lǐ hùlǐle yéye bàn gè yuè.
examples.english: She looked after her grandfather in the hospital for two weeks.

examples.hanzi: 洗完头发以后,要用护发素护理一下。
examples.pinyin: Xǐwán tóufa yǐhòu, yào yòng hùfàsù hùlǐ yíxià.
examples.english: After washing your hair, use conditioner to take care of it.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, from 肉) — marks body parts, as in 肚 belly, 脸 face, 腿 leg; 肾 is the kidney.

example.hanzi: 他的肾不太好。
example.pinyin: Tā de shèn bù tài hǎo.
example.english: His kidneys aren't in great shape.
example.fact: In everyday talk 肾 is also a cultural term: traditional Chinese medicine treats the kidney as the store of vitality, so 肾虚 ('kidney deficiency') is a very common worry. As a food ingredient, kidneys are often called 腰子.

examples.hanzi: 多喝水对肾有好处。
examples.pinyin: Duō hē shuǐ duì shèn yǒu hǎochù.
examples.english: Drinking more water is good for your kidneys.

examples.hanzi: 医生说他的肾功能正常。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō tā de shèn gōngnéng zhèngcháng.
examples.english: The doctor says his kidney function is normal.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and place, as in 道 way, 过 pass, 近 near; the radical hints at "here / this way". The 文 part is not a useful sound clue.
日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 住; 候 means to wait for someone.
侯 (hóu) is a close sound clue for hòu; it also gives 猴 hóu monkey and 喉 hóu throat.

example.hanzi: 这时候,天突然下起了大雨。
example.pinyin: Zhè shíhou, tiān tūrán xiàqǐ le dàyǔ.
example.english: At this moment, it suddenly started raining heavily.
example.fact: The wettest place on Earth by average annual rainfall is Mawsynram, India, which receives roughly 11,872 millimeters, about 39 feet, of rain per year. The extreme rainfall is driven by monsoon winds funneled through the Khasi Hills.

examples.hanzi: 这时候我才明白他的意思。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shíhou wǒ cái míngbai tā de yìsi.
examples.english: Only at that moment did I understand what he meant.

examples.hanzi: 你这时候打电话来,有什么事吗?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhè shíhou dǎ diànhuà lái, yǒu shénme shì ma?
examples.english: Why are you calling at this time? Is something up?

components.note: 来 (come) — it began as a picture of a wheat plant; the sound was borrowed for "come". 麦 (wheat) still shows it, with a root 夂 added.
讠 (speech) — 讠 is the simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 讲 is to talk and explain.
井 (jǐng) — near sound — 讲 is jiǎng; the old form had a different right side, so this is only a loose hint.

example.hanzi: 对我来讲,健康比金钱更重要。
example.pinyin: Duì wǒ láijiǎng, jiànkāng bǐ jīnqián gèng zhòngyào.
example.english: For me, health is more important than money.
example.fact: Studies of residents on Okinawa, Japan, one of the world's original 'Blue Zones', found unusually high rates of people living past 100. Researchers attributed this partly to a traditionally plant-heavy diet, strong community ties, and staying physically active well into old age.

examples.hanzi: 对小孩来讲,睡觉很重要。
examples.pinyin: Duì xiǎohái láijiǎng, shuìjiào hěn zhòngyào.
examples.english: For small children, sleep is very important.

examples.hanzi: 一般来讲,周末的人比较多。
examples.pinyin: Yìbān láijiǎng, zhōumò de rén bǐjiào duō.
examples.english: Generally speaking, there are more people on weekends.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — passing things along, as in 道 road, 送 send, 过 pass.
弟 (dì) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 第 dì and 梯 tī.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 线, 组; 给 is to supply thread, then to give.
合 (hé) is only a loose sound clue; same part in 答 dá, 拾 shí, 恰 qià.

example.hanzi: 她把钥匙递给了邻居。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ yàoshi dìgěile línjū.
example.english: She handed the key to her neighbor.
example.fact: The oldest known lock and key mechanism, made of wood, was discovered in the ruins of Nineveh and dates back roughly 4,000 years. Its pin-based design is essentially the same principle used in most modern pin-tumbler locks today.

examples.hanzi: 请把盐递给我一下。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yán dìgěi wǒ yíxià.
examples.english: Please pass me the salt.

examples.hanzi: 老师把试卷递给了每个同学。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ shìjuàn dìgěile měi gè tóngxué.
examples.english: The teacher handed the test paper to each student.

components.note: 纟 (silk, simplified 糸) — fine threads, hence delicate; also in 红 red, 级 level.
千 (qiān) gives only a rough sound for xiān.
纟 (silk thread, from 糸) — marks thread and ties, as in 线, 红, 约; 维 is a rope that holds things together.
隹 (zhuī, short-tailed bird) is only a loose sound clue for wéi, as in 推 tuī and 谁 shéi.

example.hanzi: 全麦面包含有丰富的纤维。
example.pinyin: Quánmài miànbāo hányǒu fēngfù de xiānwéi.
example.english: Whole wheat bread is rich in fiber.
example.fact: Spider silk, a natural protein fiber, has a tensile strength comparable to steel of the same diameter while being far more elastic. Some species' silk can stretch to nearly 40% of its length before breaking, a combination scientists have long tried to replicate synthetically.

examples.hanzi: 芹菜和菠菜里有很多纤维。
examples.pinyin: Qíncài hé bōcài lǐ yǒu hěn duō xiānwéi.
examples.english: Celery and spinach contain lots of fiber.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服是用天然纤维做的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu shì yòng tiānrán xiānwéi zuò de.
examples.english: This garment is made from natural fibers.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 进: to go and pick.
先 (xiān) is a close sound clue for xuǎn; 先 also in 洗 xǐ.
中 (middle) — a line through the middle of a box, a centre mark. 中 gives sound to 钟 zhōng, 种 zhǒng, 忠 zhōng and 衷 zhōng.

example.hanzi: 委员会最终选中了这个设计方案。
example.pinyin: Wěiyuánhuì zuìzhōng xuǎnzhòngle zhège shèjì fāng'àn.
example.english: The committee finally selected this design proposal.
example.fact: The Sydney Opera House's now-iconic sail-like design, selected in a 1957 international competition, was initially considered nearly impossible to build with the construction technology of the time. Engineers spent years in trial and error before the structure could finally be completed.

examples.hanzi: 老师选中了我来回答这个问题。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī xuǎnzhòngle wǒ lái huídá zhège wèntí.
examples.english: The teacher picked me to answer this question.

examples.hanzi: 这件衣服我一眼就选中了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu wǒ yì yǎn jiù xuǎnzhòng le.
examples.english: I picked out this garment at first glance.

components.note: 马 (horse) — 马 is the horse radical, as in 骗, 驾, 验; 骑 is to ride.
奇 (qí) — same sound — 骑 is qí, like 奇; 奇 also sounds out 椅 yǐ.
马 (horse) — a galloping horse. As a radical it marks horses: 骑 ride, 驾 drive. It gives sound to 妈 mā, 吗 ma, 骂 mà and 码 mǎ.

example.hanzi: 孩子们喜欢在农场骑马。
example.pinyin: Háizimen xǐhuan zài nóngchǎng qímǎ.
example.english: The kids like to ride horses on the farm.
example.fact: Horses were first domesticated by humans on the Eurasian steppes roughly 5,500 years ago. Their speed and stamina in transportation and warfare are considered one of the most transformative technological shifts in early human history, comparable in impact to the invention of the wheel.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们去草原骑马。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù cǎoyuán qímǎ.
examples.english: This weekend we're going horseback riding on the grassland.

examples.hanzi: 他骑马的姿势很标准。
examples.pinyin: Tā qímǎ de zīshì hěn biāozhǔn.
examples.english: His posture when riding a horse is very proper.

components.note: 皿 (dish) — 皿 is a vessel, as in 盘, 盒; 盗 is coveting what is not yours.
次 (drool) — 次 here originally pictured drooling — wanting something greedily.
穴 (cave, hole) — creeping in through a hole; also in 空 empty, 窗 window.
切 (qiè) gives the exact sound.

example.hanzi: 这家银行发生了一起盗窃案。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā yínháng fāshēngle yī qǐ dàoqiè'àn.
example.english: A theft occurred at this bank.
example.fact: In 1911, the Mona Lisa was stolen from the Louvre by an Italian handyman named Vincenzo Peruggia, who kept it hidden in his apartment for over two years. He was caught only after trying to sell it to an art dealer in Florence, and the theft made the painting far more famous than it had been before.

examples.hanzi: 小偷因为盗窃被警察抓住了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu yīnwèi dàoqiè bèi jǐngchá zhuāzhù le.
examples.english: The thief was caught by the police for stealing.

examples.hanzi: 他因盗窃罪被判了两年。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīn dàoqièzuì bèi pànle liǎng nián.
examples.english: He was sentenced to two years for theft.

components.note: 當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
真 (zhēn) is a sound clue for 镇 zhèn and 慎 shèn; 真 means real, true.

example.hanzi: 他说的话你别当真。
example.pinyin: Tā shuō de huà nǐ bié dàngzhēn.
example.english: Don't take what he said seriously.
example.fact: In 1938, Orson Welles's radio adaptation of 'The War of the Worlds' was presented in a realistic news-bulletin format. While later accounts of mass nationwide panic were exaggerated by newspapers, some listeners who tuned in late genuinely mistook the fictional Martian invasion for a real news broadcast.

examples.hanzi: 我是开玩笑的,你千万别当真。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì kāi wánxiào de, nǐ qiānwàn bié dàngzhēn.
examples.english: I was joking; don't take it seriously.

examples.hanzi: 你当真要辞职吗?再想想吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ dàngzhēn yào cízhí ma? Zài xiǎngxiang ba.
examples.english: Are you really going to resign? Think it over.

components.note: 将 (jiāng) is the trimmed top part: 奖 jiǎng sounds like 桨 jiǎng and 浆 jiāng.
口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.

example.hanzi: 冠军获得了一份丰厚的奖品。
example.pinyin: Guànjūn huòdéle yī fèn fēnghòu de jiǎngpǐn.
example.english: The champion received a generous prize.
example.fact: The Nobel Prize, first awarded in 1901, was funded by dynamite inventor Alfred Nobel's fortune. He reportedly restructured his will after reading a premature obituary that labeled him a 'merchant of death', choosing instead to reward achievements that benefited humanity.

examples.hanzi: 抽奖的奖品是一台新电视。
examples.pinyin: Chōujiǎng de jiǎngpǐn shì yì tái xīn diànshì.
examples.english: The raffle prize is a new TV.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们都想得到老师发的奖品。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen dōu xiǎng dédào lǎoshī fā de jiǎngpǐn.
examples.english: The children all want to get the prizes the teacher hands out.

components.note: 公 (public) — 八 over 厶: dividing 八 what is private 厶; so "shared, public, fair".
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 这位公子出身名门望族。
example.pinyin: Zhè wèi gōngzǐ chūshēn míngmén wàngzú.
example.english: This young nobleman came from a distinguished family.
example.fact: In feudal Europe, primogeniture, the practice of the eldest son inheriting the family's full estate and title, became widespread by the medieval period. It was partly meant to prevent large landholdings from being fragmented across multiple heirs, concentrating wealth and political power in a single line.

examples.hanzi: 古代戏里的公子,常常是穿着长袍的年轻人。
examples.pinyin: Gǔdài xì lǐ de gōngzǐ, chángcháng shì chuānzhe chángpáo de niánqīng rén.
examples.english: The young masters in ancient dramas are often young men in long robes.

examples.hanzi: 这位公子风度翩翩,很受欢迎。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi gōngzǐ fēngdù piānpiān, hěn shòu huānyíng.
examples.english: This young gentleman is elegant and popular.

components.note: 夕 (evening, night) — night and time: 外, 多, 夜; dreams come at night, so 夕 is the meaning clue; 林 is only filler.
予 (give) — 幻 is 予 written reversed — giving turned around, an illusion.

example.hanzi: 这座城堡看起来像梦幻中的场景。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngbǎo kànqǐlái xiàng mènghuàn zhōng de chǎngjǐng.
example.english: This castle looks like a scene from a dream.
example.fact: Neuschwanstein Castle in Bavaria, completed in the late 19th century for the reclusive King Ludwig II, was built purely as a private retreat rather than a fortress. It later became the direct visual inspiration for Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle.

examples.hanzi: 这个游乐园的夜景像梦幻一样美。
examples.pinyin: Zhège yóulèyuán de yèjǐng xiàng mènghuàn yíyàng měi.
examples.english: This amusement park looks dreamlike at night.

examples.hanzi: 她梦想过一个梦幻般的婚礼。
examples.pinyin: Tā mèngxiǎngguò yí gè mènghuàn bān de hūnlǐ.
examples.english: She dreamed of a fairy-tale wedding.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
疋 (foot) — the lower right. Dictionary story: an old man walking 疋 with a cane. Early forms show a person looking around, unsure. Treat as a memory aid.
矢 (arrow) — Dictionary reads it as a cane held by an old man; memory aid: an old man leaning on a stick, unsure which way — doubt, 怀疑.

example.hanzi: 他无疑是这个领域最优秀的专家。
example.pinyin: Tā wúyí shì zhège lǐngyù zuì yōuxiù de zhuānjiā.
example.english: He is undoubtedly the best expert in this field.
example.fact: Malcolm Gladwell's popularized '10,000-hour rule' was based on research by psychologist Anders Ericsson studying violinists. Ericsson himself later clarified that the figure was an oversimplified average, since the practice needed to reach elite performance actually varies widely by field and individual.

examples.hanzi: 这样做无疑是对的。
examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò wúyí shì duì de.
examples.english: Doing it this way is undoubtedly right.

examples.hanzi: 他无疑会成为一名优秀的老师。
examples.pinyin: Tā wúyí huì chéngwéi yì míng yōuxiù de lǎoshī.
examples.english: He will undoubtedly become an excellent teacher.
